title: Kashmir
hook: walnuts soaking in pots of water through Shiva's great night, then handed out to the neighbors

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kashmir, and the spring at Tulmul where pilgrims bring rice pudding and read the color of the water. This week ran from the Varkari walkers of Maharashtra up into the valley. Which picture from it are you keeping? Day one thousand three hundred ninety-three.

A kitchen in winter. On a clean cloth, a row of pots, filled to the brim with water, and in the water, walnuts, still in their shells. Someone has drawn on the pots and hung flowers around their necks. The family will sit up with them tonight, singing, worshiping, keeping the lamp going. And in a day or two, those walnuts will be soft from the water and on their way to every relative and neighbor on the list. Today, the last of our Kashmir days: Herath, Shiva's great night, kept the Kashmiri way.
screen: `POTS OF WATER AND WALNUTS` → `A NIGHT KEPT AWAKE` → `HERATH`

segments.voice: First, the night. Mahashivaratri, the great night of Shiva, is kept with fasting and worship and staying awake. Kashmiri Pandits keep it too, and they call it Herath. In their tradition it's a night kept at home, around the family, more than at a temple. Second, the pots. The family sets out a pot and smaller vessels, filled with water and walnuts, and calls the arrangement the vatuk. It's worshiped as Shiva and the company around him. Families tell the meaning in different ways. Some speak of Shiva's wedding to Parvati, with the pots as the wedding guests. Others speak of Bhairava, a fierce form of Shiva, appearing as light. Nobody has to settle it tonight. The water, the flowers and the lamp do their work either way. Third, the walnuts. When the worship is over, the soaked walnuts become prasad, a blessed gift, and they're shared out: to grandparents, to cousins, to the family next door. In the days after, people visit each other with greetings. So the night that begins alone with God ends at other people's doors. Now look back over this week. The Varkari reaching Pandharpur and turning for home. Then Kashmir: a lake drained, a river of kings, a theater, a recognition, a spring that a community watches. And last, a holy night with a kitchen at its center, and walnuts carried out the door. What could you share today, from what you've been given?

segments.voice: Two minutes of a small night watch. Sit, and let the room go quiet, the way a house goes quiet late on Herath. Bring to mind a lamp burning steadily. Each time your thoughts wander, come back to the lamp. Then, near the end of the sit, think of three people you'd hand a walnut to, if you had a bowl of them here. See each face for one breath. If you pray, you can say om namah shivaya, slowly, under the breath. The bell holds the time.
Kashmir. Today, Herath, Shiva's great night kept by Kashmiri Pandits, with pots of water and walnuts that become a gift for the neighbors. Today's word.
Your line: Kashmir. Today, share something small from your own kitchen or your own day with someone nearby, the way the walnuts go door to door. Day one thousand three hundred ninety-three.

howItsDone: Kashmiri Pandit families keep Herath at home with an overnight worship of the vatuk, pots of water and walnuts honored as Shiva and his company, and afterward share the soaked walnuts with relatives and neighbors as prasad.
